target_vocabulary_audit.why_that_matters: Each test is a parsing heuristic written here, and they do not agree. Separating a deity adjective from a metre name inside these strings is philological adjudication, which the owner bars from acting as identity evidence -- so the contaminated share cannot be bounded and a partial import cannot be made safe.

channels_attempted.permitted_because: an existing source-backed entity mapping: the registry was generated from the same Whitney index and records which printed spellings fold into which entity

channels_attempted.refused: :Chandas carries normalized_name and label_iast, so this join is trivially available and is barred: normalization generates candidates and cannot establish identity.
the rows are EXCEPTIONS to their hymn's ascription and say so verbatim, so the verse's existing edge names a different metre. Using it would resolve to the value the source is contradicting.

the AV registry's own header states rv_registry_name_match 'asserts nothing about whether the two indices mean the same person'. A field its author declares non-evidential cannot become evidence here.

disposition_reason: The resolution channel works -- 405 of 477 proposals resolve through the registry's own source_variants with zero ambiguity and no finding against any individual resolution. The vocabulary they resolve INTO is contaminated: an unbounded share of the AV_WHITNEY :Chandas entities are unsegmented bracket fragments carrying a deity, a metre and sometimes a verse exception in one string. Importing would record a verse's metre as a string containing a deity name, which is worse than recording no verse-level metre at all.

pre_existing_defect_found.what: 33 canonical HAS_CHANDAS edges already point at :Chandas entities that are bracket fragments rather than metre names.
pre_existing_defect_found.not_repaired_here: Re-segmenting the vocabulary re-identifies its entities, which is an owner decision and not an approved cleanup rule.
